topic: How do on-board storage constraints influence payload power allocation between immediate and time-tagged service prioritization?
consensus_response: On-board storage limitations directly impact payload power allocation, prioritizing immediate services (requiring minimal latency) over time-tagged ones.  This leads to increased interference due to limited memory buffers, forcing a tradeoff between real-time demands and potential delays in archival. To mitigate this, efficient modulation techniques like higher-order modulation schemes are crucial for improved spectral efficiency and network capacity.
reference_context: Satellite communication systems operate with limited onboard storage capacity, impacting payload power allocation.  Immediate services (requiring minimal latency) are prioritized over time-tagged ones due to the constraints of on-board memory. This prioritization necessitates efficient modulation techniques for improved spectral efficiency and network capacity.
